items.name: Binary to decimal
items.body:
`value = value * 2 + bit;`
For each bit, left to right, starting with `value = 0`

items.name: 2’s complement
items.note: Used for negative numbers

items.name: Positional value (any base)
items.note: r = base; each digit d is from 0 to r - 1
items.body:
`value = value * r + d;`
For each digit d, left to right, starting with `value = 0`

items.name: Positional value with fraction
items.note: (101.11)₂ = 5.75. Math.pow returns a double, so nothing is lost; d / r with ints would give 0
items.body: Whole part as above. After the point, digit number k (from 1) adds `d / Math.pow(r, k)`

items.name: Digits of a base-r system
items.note: Binary 0-1; octal 0-7; decimal 0-9; hexadecimal 0-9 and A-F

items.name: Decimal to base r (integer part)
items.note: With ints, n / r drops the fraction, which is what this needs
items.body:
`d = n % r;`
`n = n / r;`
Repeat until `n == 0`, then read the remainders from last to first

items.name: Decimal fraction to base r
items.note: Stop when f becomes 0; e.g. 0.625 = (0.101)₂. The cast is what takes the whole part
items.body:
`f = f * r;`
`d = (int) f;`
`f = f - d;`
The values of d, top to bottom, are the digits after the point

items.name: Binary to octal
items.note: Pad with 0s on the left of integer part / right of fraction part
items.body: Group bits in 3s from the binary point; each group → one octal digit

items.name: Binary to hexadecimal
items.note: Pad with 0s as for octal; e.g. 1011 0110 = (B6)₁₆
items.body: Group bits in 4s from the binary point; each group → one hex digit

items.name: Octal to binary
items.body: Replace each octal digit by its 3-bit binary code

items.name: Hexadecimal to binary
items.body: Replace each hex digit by its 4-bit binary code

items.name: Octal to decimal
items.body:
`value = value * 8 + d;`
For each octal digit d, left to right

items.name: Hexadecimal to decimal
items.body:
`value = value * 16 + d;`
For each hex digit d, left to right

items.name: Octal and hexadecimal interconversion
items.note: Go through binary using 3-bit and 4-bit groups

items.name: Any base to any base
items.note: Expand in base a by positional value, then divide repeatedly by b

items.name: Largest number and count in n digits
items.note: 8-bit binary: largest 255, total 256 patterns. Math.pow returns a double, so cast with (int) to store it in an int
items.body:
Largest n-digit number in base r: `Math.pow(r, n) - 1`
Distinct n-digit strings: `Math.pow(r, n)`

items.name: Bits needed for N distinct values
items.note: The smallest n with Math.pow(2, n) >= N; e.g. 100 distinct symbols need 7 bits

items.name: Binary digits needed for decimal N
items.note: N >= 1; e.g. 100 needs 7 bits (1100100). The cast drops the fraction: 6.64 becomes 6

items.name: Shift and multiply by 2
items.note: Same as multiplying/dividing by the base in decimal

items.name: Binary form of a power of 2, and one less
items.body:
`1 << k` in binary: a 1 followed by k zeros
`(1 << k) - 1` in binary: k ones

items.name: Binary subtraction rules
items.note: Borrowing from the next column turns 0 into 10, and 10-1 = 1

items.name: Binary multiplication rules
items.note: Shift-and-add: one shifted copy of multiplicand per 1 in the multiplier

items.name: Addition in base r
items.note: Applies to binary, octal and hexadecimal. s / r is integer division, which is what gives the carry
items.body:
`s = a + b + carry;`
`digit = s % r;`
`carry = s / r;`

items.name: Subtraction in base r
items.note: Borrow from the next column adds r to the current digit
items.body:
`if (a < b + borrow) { d = a + r - b - borrow; borrow = 1; }`
`else { d = a - b - borrow; borrow = 0; }`

items.name: Multiplication in base r
items.note: Integers only; carry = floor(product / r)
items.body: Multiply digit by digit in base r; add shifted partial products in base r

items.name: r's complement
items.note: r=2: 2's complement; r=10: 10's complement

items.name: (r-1)'s complement
items.note: Subtract every digit from r-1; r=2: 1's complement; r=10: 9's complement

items.name: 1's complement (numeric form)
items.note: Equals bitwise inversion; r's complement = (r-1)'s complement + 1

items.name: 2's complement (numeric form)
items.note: Represents -N in an n-bit register

items.name: 2's complement shortcut
items.body:
Copy bits from the right up to and including the first 1;
invert all bits to its left

items.name: Double complement
items.note: Complementing twice returns the original number
items.body: The 2's complement of the 2's complement of N is N

items.name: Subtraction by 2's complement
items.note: Use the same number of bits for A and B
items.body:
A - B is A + (2's complement of B)
Carry out: discard the carry, the result is positive
No carry: the result is -(2's complement of the sum)

items.name: Subtraction by 1's complement
items.body:
A - B is A + (1's complement of B)
Carry out: add it back (end-around carry), the result is positive
No carry: the result is -(1's complement of the sum)

items.name: Decimal analogy: 10's complement subtraction
items.note: Same idea as binary: add the complement, discard the carry
items.body: A - B is A + (10's complement of B), then drop the final carry

items.name: Range of n-bit unsigned integer
items.note: 8 bits: 0 to 255

items.name: Range of n-bit 2's complement integer
items.note: 8 bits: -128 to 127; only one zero

items.name: Range of n-bit 1's complement / sign-magnitude
items.note: 8 bits: -127 to 127; has both +0 and -0

items.name: Value of a 2's complement number
items.note: MSB has negative weight; e.g. 1111 1111 = -1
items.body:
`V = -b[n - 1] * Math.pow(2, n - 1);`
Then for each i from 0 to n - 2: `V += b[i] * Math.pow(2, i);`

items.name: Sign-magnitude representation
items.body:
`MSB == 0`: positive; `MSB == 1`: negative
The other `n - 1` bits hold the magnitude

items.name: Overflow in signed addition
items.note: Adding numbers of opposite signs can never overflow
items.body: Overflow when both operands have the same sign and the result has the opposite sign

items.name: Width of a sum
items.note: Extra bit is the final carry
items.body: Sum of two n-bit numbers needs at most `n+1` bits

items.name: Characters from m-bit code
items.note: 7-bit ASCII: 128; 8-bit extended ASCII / ISCII: 256

items.name: Extended ASCII
items.note: Codes 128-255 vary by code page

items.name: ASCII codes of space and line feed
items.body:
Space is `32`
Line feed `'\n'` is `10`
Carriage return `'\r'` is `13`

items.name: Case conversion by ASCII value
items.note: 'a' - 'A' is 32. The cast is needed: char + int is an int

items.name: Digit character to digit value
items.note: The result is an int, as char arithmetic always is

items.name: Alphabet position of a letter
items.note: A or a = 1, ..., Z or z = 26

items.name: Limitation of ASCII
items.note: It cannot represent Indian or other world scripts; hence ISCII and Unicode
items.body: ASCII has only 128 symbols (English letters, digits, punctuation, control codes)

items.name: ISCII
items.note: BIS standard IS 13194:1991, covers Brahmi-derived scripts
items.body:
ISCII: 8-bit, 256 codes; codes 0-127 same as ASCII, codes
128-255 for Indian scripts

items.name: Unicode code space
items.note: Every character gets a unique code point, in any language

items.name: Unicode encoding forms
items.note: UTF-8 is backward compatible with ASCII
items.body: UTF-8: 1 to 4 bytes; UTF-16: 2 or 4 bytes; UTF-32: 4 bytes

items.name: Unicode and ASCII
items.note: First 128 Unicode code points match ASCII
items.body: U+0000 to U+007F is ASCII (0 to 127)

items.name: Unicode in Java
items.note: Java strings are Unicode, so local-language text can be used

items.name: Size of encoded text
items.note: ASCII: 8 bits (1 byte) per character in memory

units.name: 3. Propositional logic, Hardware implementation, Arithmetic operations

items.name: NAND as NOT
items.note: Universal gate

items.name: Binary sum bit
items.note: Full adder

items.name: Logical connectives
items.body:
$\begin{aligned}&\sim p:\text{ not},\quad p\wedge q:\text{ and},\quad p\vee q:\text{ or},\quad p\Rightarrow q:\text{ implies},\\&p\Leftrightarrow q:\text{ iff}\end{aligned}$
`!p, p && q, p || q`

items.name: Conjunction (AND) truth values
items.latex: T\wedge T=T,\ \ T\wedge F=F,\ \ F\wedge T=F,\ \ F\wedge F=F
items.note: True only when both operands are true

items.name: Disjunction (OR) truth values
items.latex: T\vee T=T,\ \ T\vee F=T,\ \ F\vee T=T,\ \ F\vee F=F
items.note: False only when both operands are false

items.name: Implication truth values
items.latex: T\Rightarrow T=T,\ \ T\Rightarrow F=F,\ \ F\Rightarrow T=T,\ \ F\Rightarrow F=T
items.note: False only when antecedent is true and consequent is false

items.name: Biconditional truth values
items.latex: T\Leftrightarrow T=T,\ \ T\Leftrightarrow F=F,\ \ F\Leftrightarrow T=F,\ \ F\Leftrightarrow F=T
items.note: True only when both sides have the same truth value

items.name: Well-formed formula (wff) rules
items.latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{(i) a propositional variable, }T\text{ or }F\text{ is a wff}\\&\text{(ii) if }P\text{ is a wff then }\sim P\text{ is a wff}\\&\text{(iii) if }P,Q\text{ are wffs then }(P\wedge Q),(P\vee Q),(P\Rightarrow Q),(P\Leftrightarrow Q)\text{ are wffs}\\&\text{(iv) nothing else is a wff}\end{aligned}

items.name: Tautology (valid formula)
items.note: Last column of its truth table is all T

items.name: Contradiction (unsatisfiable formula)
items.note: Last column of its truth table is all F

items.name: Satisfiable and contingent formula
items.latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{Satisfiable: }T\text{ under at least one interpretation;\ contingent: }\\&\text{both }T\text{ and }F\text{ occur}\end{aligned}

items.name: Logical equivalence
items.latex: P\equiv Q\iff(P\Leftrightarrow Q)\text{ is a tautology}
items.note: Equivalent wffs have identical truth-table columns

items.name: Precedence of connectives
items.note: Usual convention (highest first); use brackets when in doubt

items.name: Statements to wff (1)
items.latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{if }p\text{ then }q\ ;\ p\text{ only if }q\ ;\ q\text{ if }p\ \to\ p\Rightarrow q\\&p\text{ if and only if }q\ \to\ p\Leftrightarrow q\end{aligned}

items.name: Statements to wff (2)
items.latex: \begin{aligned}&p\text{ and }q\ ;\ p\text{ but }q\ \to\ p\wedge q\\&\text{neither }p\text{ nor }q\ \to\ \sim p\wedge\sim q\\&p\text{ unless }q\ \to\ \sim q\Rightarrow p\ \equiv\ p\vee q\end{aligned}

items.name: AND from NAND

items.name: OR from NAND
items.note: 3 NAND gates

items.name: OR from NOR
items.note: NOR followed by a NOR used as NOT (2 gates)

items.name: AND from NOR
items.note: 3 NOR gates

items.note: 4 NAND gates: OR, then NOT

items.name: NAND from NOR
items.note: 4 NOR gates: AND, then NOT

items.name: XOR from NAND gates
items.note: 4 NAND gates

items.name: Universal gates
items.latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{NAND and NOR are universal: NOT, AND and OR can each be built }\\&\text{using only NAND (or only NOR)}\end{aligned}

items.name: NAND and NOR are not associative
items.latex: (A\uparrow B)\uparrow C\neq A\uparrow(B\uparrow C),\qquad(A\downarrow B)\downarrow C\neq A\downarrow(B\downarrow C)

units.name: 4. Introduction to Object Oriented Programming using Java

items.name: Class declaration
items.note: Class = blueprint combining data (attributes) and methods (behaviour)

items.name: main method signature
items.note: Entry point; static so it runs before any object exists

items.name: Creating an object
items.note: new allocates memory and calls the constructor

items.name: Compile and run
items.note: javac = compiler; java launches the JVM, which interprets bytecode

items.name: Java translation chain
items.note: Bytecode is portable: same .class runs on any machine with a JVM
items.body: source (.java) → javac → bytecode (.class) → JVM → machine code

items.name: Access specifiers
items.note: Order of visibility: public > protected > default > private
items.body:
`public`: everywhere
`protected`: same package + subclasses default (none): same package
`private`: same class only

items.name: Principles of OOP
items.body:
Abstraction, Encapsulation (data hiding), Inheritance (reuse),
Polymorphism (many forms)

items.name: Encapsulation rule
items.note: Binds data and methods; hides data from outside access

items.name: Identifier rules
items.note: Valid: sum_1, $x; invalid: 1sum, class
items.body:
Letters, digits, `_` and `$`; cannot start with a digit;
case-sensitive; not a keyword

items.name: Escape sequences
items.body:
` n`: new line, ` t`: tab, ` b`: backspace, ` r`: return, ` \`:
backslash, ` "`: double quote, ` '`: single quote

items.name: Object
items.note: State + behaviour + identity
items.body: An object is data (attributes) plus behaviour (methods); an instance of a class

items.name: Class versus object
items.note: One class can have any number of objects
items.body:
Class: blueprint (no memory for data until instantiated);
object: real instance (memory allocated)

items.name: Reference variable
items.note: A variable of class type holds a reference, not the object itself
items.body: `Student s;` (null reference); `s = new Student();` (refers to object)

items.name: Accessing members
items.note: Dot operator on an object reference

items.name: Reference assignment (aliasing)
items.note: Change through a is visible through b
items.body: `b = a;` ⇒ both refer to the same object (no copy is made)

items.name: Null reference
items.note: Object with no reference is eligible for garbage collection

items.name: Java Virtual Machine
items.note: "Write once, run anywhere"
items.body: JVM: a software machine that executes bytecode (.class), which makes Java platform independent

items.name: Types of errors
items.note: Logical errors give wrong output without any error message
items.body: Compile-time (syntax) error, run-time error (exception), logical error

items.name: try-catch-finally syntax
items.note: finally runs whether or not an exception occurs
items.body:
`try { risky code }`
`catch (ExceptionType e) { handler }`
`finally { always executed }`

items.name: throw and throws
items.note: throw raises an exception; throws declares that a method may pass it on

items.name: Order of catch blocks
items.note: Only the first matching catch block executes
items.body: Specific exception types first, general (e.g. `Exception`) last

items.name: Exception class hierarchy
items.note: Checked: must be caught or declared; unchecked: RuntimeException and subclasses

items.name: Division by zero in Java
items.body:
`int`: `x / 0` and `x % 0` throw `ArithmeticException`
`double`: `x / 0.0` is `Infinity` or `-Infinity`, and `0.0 / 0.0` is `NaN`
items.note: The same division behaves differently by type: an int zero throws, a double zero does not

items.name: finally always executes
items.body: `finally` runs even after `return`; skipped only by `System.exit()`

items.name: Propagation of an exception
items.body: Uncaught exception moves up the call stack until a matching catch is found; else the program terminates

items.name: long
items.note: Literal needs suffix L, e.g. 5000000000L

items.name: float
items.note: Literal needs suffix f, e.g. 3.14f

items.name: boolean

items.name: Range of an n-bit signed integer type
items.note: Sizes: byte 8, short 16, int 32, long 64

`byte, short, int, long`: 0; `float, double`: 0.0
`char`: `' u0000'`; `boolean`: `false`; objects: `null`

items.note: Invalid text throws NumberFormatException

items.note: MIN_VALUE of Double/Float is positive, unlike Integer.MIN_VALUE

items.note: Integer values -128 to 127 are cached, so == may seem to work for small values

items.name: Character classification methods
items.note: All return boolean

items.name: Character case conversion
items.note: Returns a char; non-letters are returned unchanged

items.name: Character.getNumericValue
items.note: Digits and letters give their value in base up to 36

items.note: Automatic, no loss of range

items.note: Keeps only the low-order bits of the value

items.body: byte, short, char→`int`; then if any operand is long/float/double, result is that widest type

items.note: char in arithmetic is promoted to int; cast back to get a char

items.note: Assigning a wider type to a narrower one needs an explicit cast

items.name: Variable declaration
items.note: Declare with a type; the type constrains the values it can hold

items.name: Named constant
items.note: final: value assigned once and cannot change; convention is UPPER_CASE

items.body: Primitive variable stores the value; object variable stores a reference to the object

items.note: Without a temporary: a = a + b; b = a - b; a = a - b;

items.note: % gives the remainder; / on two ints gives an int

items.note: Sign of result follows the dividend; also works on floating-point numbers

items.note: Holds for int a and b != 0, because a / b is integer division. It fails for doubles

items.note: Result type is the widest operand type, evaluated left to right

items.name: Pre-increment and pre-decrement

items.name: Post-increment and post-decrement

items.name: x = x++ leaves x unchanged

items.body: `x = x++;` ⇒ x keeps its old value

items.name: Compound assignment operators
items.body:
`x += y`, `x -= y`, `x *= y`, `x /= y`, `x %= y`
Each is `x = x op y`, with a hidden cast back to the type of x

items.name: Relational operators
items.note: Result is boolean; == on objects compares references

items.name: Short-circuit evaluation
items.note: Non-short-circuit forms & and | evaluate both operands
items.body: `a && b`: b evaluated only if a is true; `a || b`: b evaluated only if a is false

items.body:
`!(a && b)` is the same as `!a || !b`
`!(a || b)` is the same as `!a && !b`

items.name: Ternary operator
items.note: Gives expr1 if condition is true, else expr2; e.g. max = a > b ? a : b;

items.name: Ternary as if-else
items.note: Ternary is right-associative: a ? b : c ? d : e = a ? b : (c ? d : e)
items.body: `x = c ? p : q;` is the same as `if (c) x = p; else x = q;`

items.name: Operator precedence in Java
items.note: Highest to lowest, top to bottom (shift and bitwise operators omitted)

items.name: Associativity of operators
items.note: e.g. a = b = c = 5 assigns right to left
items.body: Left to right: most binary operators; right to left: unary operators, assignment, ternary

items.name: String concatenation with +
items.note: + is left to right; once a String appears, the rest is concatenated

items.name: Math formula to Java expression
items.note: Brackets are needed; use 2.0 or a cast to avoid integer division

items.name: Temperature conversion trap
items.note: 9 / 5 with ints is 1, which gives the wrong answer. Write 9.0 / 5 or (9 * c) / 5.0

items.name: Math class basics
items.note: No import needed and no object is created

items.name: Math.pow
items.note: a to the power b. pow(x, 0) = 1; pow(x, 0.5) = sqrt(x); pow(x, -1) = 1 / x. Returns a double, so int y = Math.pow(2, 3) needs a cast

items.name: Math.sqrt
items.note: NaN if x < 0. Returns a double, so storing it in an int needs a cast

items.name: Math.cbrt
items.note: Cube root. Works for negative x: cbrt(-27) = -3.0

items.name: Math.abs
items.note: Return type same as argument; abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) is still negative

items.name: Math.ceil
items.note: Smallest whole number >= x, as double; ceil(-2.5) = -2.0

items.name: Math.floor
items.note: Largest whole number <= x, as double; floor(-2.5) = -3.0

items.name: Math.round
items.note: Returns long for double, int for float; round(2.5)=3, round(-2.5)=-2, round(-2.6)=-3

items.name: Math.rint
items.note: Nearest integer, ties go to the even one: rint(2.5)=2.0, rint(3.5)=4.0

items.name: Math.max and Math.min
items.note: Result type is the promoted type: max(3, 4.5) = 4.5

items.name: Math.random
items.note: From 0.0 up to, but not including, 1.0. Random integer 0 to n - 1: (int) (Math.random() * n). The brackets matter: (int) Math.random() * n is always 0

items.name: Random integer in a range
items.note: Gives an integer from a to b inclusive

items.name: Math.hypot
items.note: Length of hypotenuse

items.name: Math.exp
items.note: e to the power x

items.name: Math.log
items.note: Natural logarithm, to base e; log(0) = -Infinity; NaN for x < 0

items.name: Math.log10
items.note: Logarithm to base 10

items.name: Logarithm to any base
items.note: Logarithm of x to base b. Number of binary digits of n: (int) (Math.log(n) / Math.log(2)) + 1

items.name: Trigonometric methods
items.note: Argument x is in radians

items.name: Inverse trigonometric methods
items.note: Results are in radians; atan2(y, x) gives the angle of the point (x, y)

items.name: Return types of Math methods
items.note: Use (int) to store a double result in an int

items.name: Rounding to n decimal places
items.note: Two decimals; use Math.pow(10, n) in place of 100 for n decimals. Write 100.0, or the division drops them

items.name: Iterations of a counting loop

items.body:
`for (i = a; i < b; i += s)` runs `(b - a + s - 1) / s` times
`for (i = a; i <= b; i += s)` runs `(b - a) / s + 1` times
items.note: These rely on integer division, for positive s and b > a

items.name: Iterations of a doubling loop
items.note: A halving loop (n /= 2 while n > 0) runs the same number of times
items.body: `for (i = 1; i <= n; i *= 2)` runs `(int) (Math.log(n) / Math.log(2)) + 1` times

items.name: Iterations of nested loops
items.body:
Independent loops: `m * n` times
`for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) for (j = 1; j <= i; j++)` runs `n * (n + 1) / 2` times
items.note: Multiply first: n * (n + 1) is always even, so the division is exact

items.name: Right triangle pattern
items.body: Row i (from 1 to n) has i stars; total `n * (n + 1) / 2`

items.name: Pyramid pattern
items.body: Row i: `n - i` spaces and `2 * i - 1` stars; total stars `n * n`

items.name: Inverted triangle pattern
items.body: Row i (from 1 to n): `n - i + 1` stars

items.name: Diamond pattern
items.note: Upper half is a pyramid of n rows, lower half a pyramid of n-1 rows

items.name: Floyd's triangle
items.body: Row i has i numbers; last number in row i: `i * (i + 1) / 2`

items.name: Pascal's triangle entry
items.note: Row n has n + 1 entries, starting and ending with 1. Use long: factorials overflow int after 12!
items.body:
`fact(n) / (fact(r) * fact(n - r))`
`c(n, r) == c(n - 1, r - 1) + c(n - 1, r)`

items.note: Start rev = 0 and apply for each digit d from the right

items.note: 153 = 1*1*1 + 5*5*5 + 3*3*3; 1634 uses fourth powers of its digits

`sum += Math.pow(d, k);`
For each digit d, where k is the number of digits; n is Armstrong if `sum == n`

`if (n % d == 0) sum += d;`
For d from 1 to n - 1; n is perfect if `sum == n`

items.note: i * i <= n stops at the square root without calling Math.sqrt

items.name: Composite number
items.body: `n > 1` and has a divisor d with `1 < d && d < n`

items.body:
Twin primes: p and `p + 2` both prime
Co-prime: `gcd(a, b) == 1`

items.name: Emirp number
items.note: e.g. 13 and 31
items.body: p is prime, `reverse(p)` is prime, and `reverse(p) != p`

items.name: Automorphic number
items.note: n squared ends with n: 5, 6, 25, 76. The cast keeps the % on ints
items.body: `n * n % (int) Math.pow(10, k) == n`, where k is the number of digits of n

items.name: Special (strong) number
items.body:
`sum += fact(d);`
For each digit d; n is special if `sum == n`

items.name: Buzz number
items.note: Divisible by 7 or ends with 7: 49, 27

items.name: Magic number
items.note: 199 -> 19 -> 10 -> 1; equivalent to n % 9 == 1 for n > 0
items.body: Repeated digit sum of n ends at 1

items.name: Digital root
items.note: Repeated digit sum until one digit remains

items.name: Disarium number
items.body:
`sum += Math.pow(d, i);`
For the digit d at position i from the left, with i from 1; n is Disarium if `sum == n`

items.name: Kaprekar number
items.note: 45: 2025 splits into 20 and 25, and 20 + 25 = 45. p must be an int, or the division keeps a fraction
items.body:
`a = n * n / p;`
`b = n * n % p;`
Where `p = (int) Math.pow(10, k)` and k is the number of digits of n; `a + b == n` and `b > 0`

items.name: Tech number
items.body: `(a + b) * (a + b) == n`, where n has an even number of digits and splits into halves a and b

items.name: Happy number
items.body: Repeated sum of squares of digits reaches 1

items.name: Smith number
items.body: Composite n whose digit sum equals the digit sum of its prime factors, with repetition

items.name: Unique number

items.note: Write (a / gcd) * b to avoid int overflow

nPr: `fact(n) / fact(n - r)`

items.note: Use long, as factorials overflow int. Integer division is exact here

While `n > 0`, starting with `String bin = ""`

For the digit d at position i from the right, with i from 0

`t = t * x / k;`

For k from 1 upwards, starting with `t = 1.0` and `sum = 1.0`

items.body:
`t = -t * x * x / ((2 * k) * (2 * k + 1));`
`sum += t;`
For k from 1 upwards, starting with `t = x` and `sum = x`

`sum += t;`
For k from 1 upwards, starting with `t = 1.0` and `sum = 1.0`

`sum += sign * Math.pow(x, k) / k;`
`sign = -sign;`
For k from 1 upwards, starting with `sign = 1`

`sum += Math.pow(x, k);`
For k from 0 upwards; sum approaches `1 / (1 - x)` when `Math.abs(x) < 1`

For k from 1 to n

`}`

items.note: Keep m in a variable first, as a[j][i] changes during the loop. Use doubles: an int m would be 0 or wrong
items.body:
`double m = a[j][i] / a[i][i];`
`a[j][k] -= m * a[i][k];`
For each column k of row j, where `j > i`

items.name: Back substitution
items.note: Solve from the last equation upwards
items.body:
`sum += a[i][j] * x[j];`, for j from i + 1 to n - 1
`x[i] = (b[i] - sum) / a[i][i];`

Strings are anagrams iff their sorted characters are equal
